StackSentry v0.1.0
Target: testdata/compose/insecure.yaml (project "compose")
Scan time: 2026-10-01T12:00:00Z
Rules evaluated: 27 of 27
Services analyzed: 3
Findings: 3 critical, 10 high, 13 medium, 14 low, 2 info

CRITICAL  SST-SEC-001  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  The Docker daemon socket is mounted into the container.
  Evidence: /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
  Why this matters: Access to the Docker socket can effectively grant host-level control: anyone who
    can talk to it can start privileged containers and mount the host filesystem. Mounting it
    read-only (:ro) does not restrict API calls.
  Fix: Remove the mount unless this service explicitly requires Docker daemon access. If it does
    (for example a reverse proxy reading container labels), put a filtering socket proxy in front of
    the socket that only allows the required read-only API endpoints.

CRITICAL  SST-SEC-002  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  The service runs in privileged mode.
  Evidence: privileged: true
  Why this matters: privileged: true grants all Linux capabilities and access to all host devices
    and disables most isolation (seccomp, AppArmor/SELinux confinement). A compromise of the process
    is close to a compromise of the host.
  Fix: Remove privileged: true. Grant only the specific capabilities (cap_add) or devices (devices)
    the workload needs, and document why they are required.

CRITICAL  SST-SEC-010  portainer  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:24)
  The service appears to expose or use the Docker Engine API over unencrypted TCP.
  Evidence: port 2375:2375/tcp publishes the unencrypted Docker API port 2375 (all host interfaces)
  Confidence: medium
  Why this matters: The Docker Engine API on TCP port 2375 has neither authentication nor
    encryption. Anyone who can reach it controls the Docker host, which is equivalent to root
    access.
  Fix: Do not publish port 2375. If remote API access is required, use TLS with client certificate
    verification (port 2376, --tlsverify) or SSH (DOCKER_HOST=ssh://user@host). Keep socket proxies
    on an internal network and never publish their port.

HIGH  SST-NET-001  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)
  A database port is published on all host interfaces.
  Evidence: 5432:5432/tcp (PostgreSQL port published on all host interfaces)
  Why this matters: Published database ports are reachable from other machines and, on many Linux
    hosts, bypass host firewalls such as UFW or firewalld because Docker manages its own iptables
    rules. Databases reachable from the network are frequent targets of credential brute-forcing and
    ransom attacks.
  Fix: Remove the ports entry if only other containers need the database; they can reach it over the
    Compose network by service name. If host access is required, bind to localhost, e.g.
    "127.0.0.1:5432:5432". Exposure may be intentional, but it should be reviewed.

HIGH  SST-OPS-003  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  No restart policy is configured, so the container stays down after a crash or host reboot.
  Evidence: restart is missing
  Why this matters: Docker's default restart policy is "no". A long-running service that crashes, or
    whose host reboots, stays down until someone intervenes.
  Fix: Add: restart: unless-stopped (or always / on-failure, depending on the desired behavior).

HIGH  SST-OPS-003  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)

HIGH  SST-SEC-003  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  The service shares the host's network stack (network_mode: host).
  Evidence: network_mode: host
  Why this matters: Host networking removes normal Docker network isolation: every port the process
    opens is reachable on all host interfaces, port publishing rules no longer apply, and the
    container can reach services bound to the host's localhost.
  Fix: Use a bridge network and publish only the required ports, preferably bound to 127.0.0.1 or a
    specific interface. Keep host networking only for workloads that need it (for example some
    discovery or VPN tools) and document the exception.

HIGH  SST-SEC-004  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  The service adds Linux capabilities that significantly weaken container isolation.
  Evidence: cap_add: SYS_ADMIN (broad administrative privileges such as mounting filesystems;
              enables many escape techniques)
  Why this matters: These capabilities grant kernel-level privileges that are commonly abused for
    container escapes, for example mounting filesystems, loading kernel modules or tracing other
    processes.
  Fix: Remove the listed capabilities from cap_add unless they are strictly required. If one is
    needed, document why and combine it with cap_drop: [ALL], a non-root user and security_opt:
    [no-new-privileges:true].

HIGH  SST-SEC-007  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  A sensitive host location is bind-mounted into the container.
  Evidence: /:/host (read-write): the entire host filesystem
  Why this matters: System locations such as /, /etc, /proc, /sys, /dev, /root or /var/lib/docker
    expose host credentials, kernel interfaces, devices or other containers' data. Write access
    usually allows a full host compromise; even read access can leak secrets.
  Fix: Mount only the specific file or subdirectory the service needs, read-only where possible.
    Monitoring agents that legitimately need /proc or /sys should mount them read-only and be
    reviewed as privileged components.

HIGH  SST-SEC-011  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  An environment variable that looks like a credential has an inline value in the Compose file.
  Evidence: API_TOKEN=********
            DB_PASSWORD=********
  Why this matters: Inline secrets end up in version control, backups, CI logs and docker inspect
    output, and are visible to everyone who can read the Compose file.
  Fix: Move the value out of the Compose file: use Docker secrets (with *_FILE variables where the
    image supports them), an external secret manager, or interpolation such as ${DB_PASSWORD} with
    the value injected at deploy time from an environment file that is not committed. Rotate the
    secret if the file was ever shared.

HIGH  SST-SEC-011  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)
  An environment variable that looks like a credential has an inline value in the Compose file.
  Evidence: POSTGRES_PASSWORD=********
  Why this matters: Inline secrets end up in version control, backups, CI logs and docker inspect
    output, and are visible to everyone who can read the Compose file.
  Fix: Move the value out of the Compose file: use Docker secrets (with *_FILE variables where the
    image supports them), an external secret manager, or interpolation such as ${DB_PASSWORD} with
    the value injected at deploy time from an environment file that is not committed. Rotate the
    secret if the file was ever shared.

HIGH  SST-STO-001  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)
  The database service has no volume mounted at its data directory.
  Evidence: no volume is mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data (PostgreSQL data directory)
  Why this matters: Without a volume the data lives in the container's writable layer and is lost
    when the container is recreated, for example by docker compose down, an image upgrade or a
    configuration change.
  Fix: Mount a named volume at the data directory, e.g. "db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data", declare
    it under the top-level volumes key and back it up regularly.

MEDIUM  SST-NET-003  portainer  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:24)
  An administration interface appears to be published on all host interfaces.
  Evidence: portainer/portainer-ce:2.21.4 publishes 9443:9443/tcp on all host interfaces (Portainer)
            portainer/portainer-ce:2.21.4 publishes 2375:2375/tcp on all host interfaces (Portainer)
  Why this matters: Admin dashboards provide powerful control over infrastructure or data.
    Publishing them broadly increases exposure to credential guessing and to vulnerabilities in the
    tool itself.
  Fix: Review the exposure. Bind the port to 127.0.0.1 and use an SSH tunnel or VPN, or put the
    interface behind a reverse proxy with strong authentication and TLS.

MEDIUM  SST-OPS-001  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  No healthcheck is defined for the service in the Compose file.
  Evidence: healthcheck is not defined
  Why this matters: Without a healthcheck Docker only knows whether the process is running, not
    whether it works. depends_on with condition: service_healthy, automated recovery and monitoring
    cannot detect a hung or misconfigured service.
  Fix: Add a healthcheck that exercises the service (for example an HTTP endpoint or a database
    ping) with sensible interval, timeout, retries and start_period values.

MEDIUM  SST-OPS-001  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)

MEDIUM  SST-OPS-005  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  The image uses a mutable tag (latest or no tag at all).
  Evidence: image: example/app:latest
  Why this matters: Mutable tags can point to a different image every time you pull. Deployments
    become non-reproducible, rollbacks unreliable, and unreviewed upstream changes can reach
    production silently.
  Fix: Pin a specific version tag (for example postgres:16.4) and update it deliberately. For full
    reproducibility also pin the digest (image: name:tag@sha256:...).

MEDIUM  SST-OPS-005  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)
  The image uses a mutable tag (latest or no tag at all).
  Evidence: image: postgres (no tag, resolves to latest)
  Why this matters: Mutable tags can point to a different image every time you pull. Deployments
    become non-reproducible, rollbacks unreliable, and unreviewed upstream changes can reach
    production silently.
  Fix: Pin a specific version tag (for example postgres:16.4) and update it deliberately. For full
    reproducibility also pin the digest (image: name:tag@sha256:...).

MEDIUM  SST-RES-003  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  Container logs are not configured to rotate.
  Evidence: logging is not configured (the daemon's default log driver applies)
  Why this matters: Docker's default json-file log driver keeps logs without limit unless max-size
    is set, so a chatty container can fill the disk.
  Fix: Configure rotation, for example logging: {driver: json-file, options: {max-size: "10m",
    max-file: "3"}}, or set log-driver/log-opts once for all containers in the Docker daemon
    configuration.

MEDIUM  SST-RES-003  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)

    configuration.

MEDIUM  SST-SEC-006  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  A host path is bind-mounted without read-only protection.
  Evidence: /:/host (read-write)
            ./data:/data (read-write)
  Why this matters: A writable bind mount lets the container modify files on the host. If the
    container is compromised, an attacker can tamper with host files, configuration or data shared
    with other services.
  Fix: Append :ro (short syntax) or set read_only: true (long syntax) for mounts the container only
    reads, such as configuration files. For data the service must write, prefer a named volume or
    make sure the host directory is dedicated to this service.

MEDIUM  SST-SEC-008  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  No user is configured, so the container runs as the image's default user, which is root for many
  images.
  Evidence: user is not set
  Why this matters: Processes running as root inside a container have more power if they escape
    isolation or write to mounted volumes. Without a user setting the effective user depends on the
    image's USER instruction, which StackSentry cannot see without pulling the image.
  Fix: Add a dedicated unprivileged user where supported by the image, e.g. user: "1000:1000" or a
    named user documented by the image (such as node). Make sure mounted volumes are writable by
    that UID.

MEDIUM  SST-SEC-008  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)

LOW  SST-OPS-004  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  The service sets a fixed container_name.
  Evidence: container_name: app
  Why this matters: Fixed container names must be unique on the host. They prevent scaling the
    service, can clash with other projects or copies of the same stack, and bypass Compose's
    project-scoped naming.
  Fix: Remove container_name and let Compose generate project-scoped names. Other services can reach
    it by its service name, which works without container_name.

LOW  SST-OPS-006  portainer  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:24)
  The image is pinned by version tag but not by digest.
  Evidence: image: portainer/portainer-ce:2.21.4 has no @sha256 digest
  Why this matters: Tags can be re-pushed by the publisher, so the same tag may resolve to different
    content over time. Pinning the digest guarantees that every deployment runs exactly the reviewed
    image. This is a reproducibility recommendation, not a security vulnerability.
  Fix: Append the digest: image: name:tag@sha256:<digest> (look it up with docker buildx imagetools
    inspect name:tag). Tools such as Renovate or Dependabot can keep digests up to date.

LOW  SST-OPS-007  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)
  No stop_grace_period is set, so Docker kills the container 10 seconds after asking it to stop.
  Evidence: stop_grace_period is not set (Docker default: 10s)
  Why this matters: Databases, queues and workflow engines may need more than 10 seconds to flush
    data, finish jobs or close connections. A forced kill can corrupt data or lose in-flight work.
  Fix: Set stop_grace_period to match the service's shutdown behavior (for example
    stop_grace_period: 30s for databases and workflow tools) and make sure the process handles
    SIGTERM or the configured stop_signal.

LOW  SST-RES-001  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  No memory limit is configured for the service.
  Evidence: deploy.resources.limits.memory and mem_limit are not set
  Why this matters: A memory leak or load spike in one container can consume all host memory and
    trigger the kernel OOM killer for unrelated processes, including other services on the host.
  Fix: Set deploy.resources.limits.memory (for example 512M) based on observed usage, or mem_limit
    for older Compose versions.

LOW  SST-RES-001  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)

LOW  SST-RES-002  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  No CPU limit is configured for the service.
  Evidence: deploy.resources.limits.cpus and cpus are not set
  Why this matters: Without a CPU limit a busy or runaway container can starve other services on the
    same host.
  Fix: Set deploy.resources.limits.cpus (for example "1.0") or cpus for older Compose versions.

LOW  SST-SEC-005  db  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:17)
  The service keeps Docker's default Linux capabilities (cap_drop does not contain ALL).
  Evidence: cap_drop is not set
  Why this matters: Docker grants containers a default capability set (for example CHOWN, SETUID,
    NET_RAW). Most applications need few or none of them. This is a hardening recommendation, not a
    defect: some images need specific capabilities to start.
  Fix: Add cap_drop: [ALL] and add back only what the service needs with cap_add (for example
    NET_BIND_SERVICE to bind ports below 1024). Test the service after the change.

LOW  SST-SEC-005  portainer  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:24)
  The service keeps Docker's default Linux capabilities (cap_drop does not contain ALL).
  Evidence: cap_drop is not set
  Why this matters: Docker grants containers a default capability set (for example CHOWN, SETUID,

LOW  SST-SEC-009  app  (testdata/compose/insecure.yaml:3)
  The container's root filesystem is writable (read_only: true is not set).
  Evidence: read_only is not set
  Why this matters: A read-only root filesystem prevents an attacker from modifying binaries or
    dropping tools inside the container and makes unexpected writes visible.
  Fix: Set read_only: true and provide writable locations explicitly with tmpfs (for example /tmp or
    /run) or volumes for application data. Many applications need some writable directories; test
    before enforcing.
